name: Territory Outbound — 15 touches / 30 days
description: Multi-modality outbound cadence. One touch every other calendar day across 30 days, weekend touches shifted to the next business day. Built on Challenger (Teach/Tailor/Take Control) with a Command of the Message spine: Warmer, Reframe, Emotional Impact, Resolution Path.

steps.name: Connect — no pitch
steps.intent: Warmer. Buy the right to challenge later. Zero ask.
steps.body: {{first_name}} — I work with {{vertical}} teams on {{reframe_short}}. Not pitching you anything here; what {{company}} is doing is directly relevant to a pattern I'm tracking. Happy to trade notes.

steps.name: Email 1 — Warmer + Reframe
steps.intent: Teach. Name the trigger, then reframe their stated problem into the real one.
steps.subject: {{company}} — a question about {{vertical}} data

steps.name: Call 1 — Reframe dial
steps.intent: Teach + Take Control. Land the Reframe live, earn one discovery answer.

talkTrack.opener: {{first_name}}, this is {{sender_name}} at Qumulo — I sent you a note Tuesday, figured I'd earn 30 seconds to say it out loud. Fair?
talkTrack.reframe: Most {{vertical}} teams I talk to are budgeting for capacity. What we see across our {{vertical}} customers is that capacity is the symptom — the actual constraint is this: {{reframe}}.
discovery: Walk me through how {{workflow}} works today end to end — where does it hurt first?
When that happens, who downstream feels it, and what does it cost them?
What had you prioritize this now versus six months ago?

objections.say: Good — most teams are, right up until {{objection_trigger}}. When's the last time you stress-tested that scenario?
Happy to. So it answers the right question: who else would need to be in the room, and what would have to be true for you to act on it?

talkTrack.voicemail: {{first_name}}, {{sender_name}} at Qumulo, {{sender_phone}}. Calling about {{reframe_short}} at {{company}} — not a capacity pitch. I'll follow up by email. {{sender_phone}}.
talkTrack.nextStep: 15 minutes on the calendar this week or next. Fallback: permission to send the {{asset_title}} and follow up in a week.

steps.name: Engage their content
steps.intent: Tailor. Be visible and specific before you DM.
steps.body:
Find {{first_name}}'s most recent post, or a {{company}} announcement from the last 30 days.

Leave ONE comment that adds a specific observation only someone who knows {{vertical}} would make. No "great post." No product mention. No link.

If they have posted nothing in 90 days, react to a {{company}} page post instead and log this touch as done.

steps.name: Email 2 — Teaching Insight
steps.intent: Commercial Teaching. Counter-intuitive, defensible, does not pitch.
steps.subject: what we're seeing across {{vertical}}

steps.name: Call 2 — Teaching Insight dial
steps.intent: Teach. Lead with the insight, not the follow-up-on-my-email apology.

talkTrack.opener: {{first_name}} — {{sender_name}} at Qumulo. I'm not calling to check if you got my email. I'm calling because of one thing in it. 30 seconds?
talkTrack.reframe: {{ti_contradiction}} That's the part most {{vertical}} teams haven't priced in yet.
discovery: Is that showing up at {{company}} yet, or are you still ahead of it?
Who owns that decision — you, or does it sit with {{pivot_persona}}?
What's your data growth rate right now, and where does it break first: capacity, performance, or the team's time?

objections.when: "We're going to do this in cloud."
objections.say: Right instinct for a lot of workloads. The question we'd ask: what does egress and re-hydration look like at full scale? That's where the math usually turns.
Understood — and the reason I'm pushing is the cost of waiting another quarter at your scale is roughly {{coi_current}}. Let's talk about what could move budget, not whether.

talkTrack.voicemail: {{first_name}}, {{sender_name}} at Qumulo. One line: {{ti_contradiction_short}} I think that's live at {{company}}. {{sender_phone}}.
talkTrack.nextStep: 15 minutes. Fallback: get one name in the buying committee.

steps.name: LinkedIn DM — the insight in three lines
steps.intent: Teach in the channel they actually read. Short enough to read on a phone.
steps.body:
{{first_name}} — three lines, no deck.

Most {{vertical}} teams believe {{ti_wisdom_short}}. What we see is {{ti_contradiction_short}}.

If that's live at {{company}}, it's worth 15 minutes. If it isn't, tell me and I'll stop.

steps.name: Email 3 — Cost of Inaction
steps.intent: COI. Put a defensible number on the status quo. Defeats "no decision".
steps.subject: the {{vertical}} number that never shows up on an invoice

steps.name: Call 3 — COI dial
steps.intent: Constructive Tension. Make the status quo expensive out loud.

talkTrack.opener: {{first_name}} — {{sender_name}}, Qumulo. I sent you a number this week and I want to know if it's wrong. Worth 60 seconds?
talkTrack.reframe: Our read is {{company}} is already paying {{coi_current}}. Over 12 months that compounds to {{coi_compounding}}, because {{coi_mechanism}}.
discovery: Where's that number wrong for you — too high, too low, or measuring the wrong thing?
If this doesn't get solved, what breaks first, and who notices?
Who'd have to see that number for it to become a funded project?

objections.say: Compared to what? The number we look at is the cost of staying where you are — that's the {{coi_current}} we just walked through.
Then help me correct it. What's the real figure? I'd rather be accurate than persuasive.

talkTrack.voicemail: {{first_name}}, {{sender_name}} at Qumulo. I put a number on the status quo at {{company}} — {{coi_current}}. I'd like to be told I'm wrong. {{sender_phone}}.
talkTrack.nextStep: A working session to correct the number with their data. That IS the meeting.

steps.name: Email 4 — Proof
steps.intent: Resolution Path. Pattern recognition and evidence, judged without you in the room.
steps.subject: {{proof_headline}}

steps.name: LinkedIn — share the asset
steps.intent: Tailor. One line of why-this-matters-to-you, then get out of the way.

steps.name: Email 5 — Message Pivot / multi-thread
steps.intent: Same value, different seat. Widen the buying committee or earn a referral.
steps.subject: {{pivot_persona}} version of this
steps.body:
{{first_name}} —

Different angle. Everything I've sent framed this as an infrastructure problem: {{reframe_short}}.

For {{pivot_persona}}, the same issue reads as {{pivot_metric}} — and that's usually the version with budget attached.

If that's the right door at {{company}}, point me at it and I'll take it there directly. Or forward this; I won't say you sent me.

{{sender_name}}

steps.name: Call 4 — Take Control dial
steps.intent: Take Control. Direct ask, no hedging. This is the one most reps skip.

talkTrack.opener: {{first_name}} — {{sender_name}} at Qumulo. Last call from me on this, and I want to use it well. Two minutes?
talkTrack.reframe: Short version: {{reframe_short}}, it's costing roughly {{coi_current}}, and {{proof_short}}.
discovery: Is this a "not now" or a "not us"? Those need different answers from me.
If it's not now — what has to happen before it is?
If it's not you — who is it?

objections.say: Happy to, and I want it to answer the right question. Who else needs to be in the conversation, and what would have to be true for you to act?
I'd rather have a clean no than a slow maybe — it's more useful to both of us. Which is it?

talkTrack.voicemail: {{first_name}}, {{sender_name}}, Qumulo, {{sender_phone}}. Last one from me — I'd rather get a clean no than keep guessing. One line back either way and I'll respect it. {{sender_phone}}.
talkTrack.nextStep: A yes, a no, or a named referral. All three are acceptable outcomes.

steps.name: LinkedIn — close the loop
steps.intent: Low-pressure permission to stop. Often outperforms the email breakup.
steps.body:
{{first_name}} — closing the loop on my end. No hard feelings if the timing's wrong.

If {{reframe_short}} becomes live at {{company}} in the next couple of quarters, I'm easy to find. I'll keep sending the {{vertical}} benchmarks that are actually useful and nothing else.

steps.name: Email 6 — Breakup, three doors
steps.intent: Permission to close. Every option is a usable answer; silence stops being one.
steps.subject: closing the file on {{company}}
steps.body:
{{first_name}} —

I've sent a few notes on {{reframe_short}}. No response is a data point, and I'd rather read it correctly than keep filling your inbox.

Three doors, any of them useful to me:

1. It matters, timing's wrong — tell me when to come back.
2. It matters, it isn't your call — point me at who owns it.
3. I've misread {{company}} — say so and I'll close the file.

For what it's worth, the reason I pushed: {{coi_current}}, compounding to {{coi_compounding}}. If that's genuinely not true at {{company}}, door 3 is the right answer and I'll take it.

{{sender_name}}
{{sender_title}} | Qumulo
